summary: Delivered the angular-super-productivity AppSpec with legs (a) create-task and (e) reload-persistence, both driven green on both lanes by calibration. Fixed the playwright-host NUL byte. Corrected three calibration contradictions, each recorded as a constant: the work-view host tag; the IndexedDB reader's localeCompare ordering, which disagreed with every schema's code-unit sortedUnique check; and the telemetry reader's refusal of the cross-origin cache member the app's own lazy externalAssets group creates on reload. Found an unrepaired migrated-lane runtime regression (split.component TypeError, 1 page error + 2 console errors per load, zero in era) and deliberately kept it OUT of the expected inventories. No drag, no legs (c)/(d), no runner, nothing published. tsc clean, lint 0 errors, 2050/2050.
open_questions: The migrated lane cannot publish until the split.component regression is repaired: witnessRecord.pageErrors must be 0 and it measures 1 per document load (2 console errors). Root cause is an @Input() set splitPos calling renderer addClass against an undefined element ref under Angular 16 input-setter timing. Repair needs packages/frameworks/** plus a lane rebuild, both outside this contract. Recorded as WITNESS_ANGULAR_SUPER_PRODUCTIVITY_MIGRATED_LANE_REGRESSION.

Two rendered-style probes genuinely differ across the lift and will need declared-difference entries at publish time: header-icon-button font-family (Roboto,"Helvetica Neue",sans-serif vs Arial) and document-body font-family (drops "Helvetica Neue"). Measured values are recorded in WITNESS_ANGULAR_SUPER_PRODUCTIVITY_MEASURED_STYLE_DIFFERENCES. Because the schema requires the two lanes' typeface records to be exactly equal, the typeface reading is anchored on side-navigation (identical in both lanes) rather than document-body; confirm that anchor choice.
